question: Can a causal-topology learner detect unannounced changes from A to B and return to A, retaining dormant source knowledge and outperforming strong recency/Bayesian controls while avoiding false rewires on stationary and random noise?
hypothesis: A local change detector with separated training-only switch witnesses and explicit source reactivation improves both changed-environment and old-environment cold-return prediction, with bounded spurious switches, over matched-information conventional online models.
changed_paths: existing G29 atlas and existing G29 CI workflow only

inputs.name: seeded synthetic six-bit causal streams
inputs.source: new deterministic local generator committed before primary execution
inputs.sha256: will refer to exact frozen run.cjs git blob on first-use; cannot prehash uncreated source

frozen_design.environment_order: Pretrain A64, then unannounced stream with 48 B training observations and 48 A-return training observations (stationary/noise controls never change). Source and target hide true parents/mapping, and policies never receive segment label.
frozen_design.splits: At each of B and return A, use independently shuffled 64 six-bit action IDs: 48 training-feedback prequential events and 16 strictly held, never learned; source A sees all 64 action IDs once. Source noise action/visit/domain separated from B/R and held. B remaps causal parents (same truth function), R reuses original A truth function and parents.
frozen_design.data_budget: Per seed A64 labeled source; two 48-event streams visible online; two disjoint-from-training 16-action evaluation sets held until scoring; all competing arms receive identical information/times; source A64 + stream96 persisted evidence = 320 bytes plus metadata within 384 bytes. No teacher.
frozen_design.compute_budget: All local graph choices evaluated only each 8 observed events, at most one edge mutation/checkpoint; each arm has its own documented work count. Strong global/Bayesian controls may use more scratch computation. No matched-compute, wall-clock, or energy gain claims.
frozen_design.capacity: All predictors use only one- to three-parent Boolean conditional tables with Laplace-smoothed counts; maximum 3 active graph edges; 384-byte serialized A and stream evidence plus mode/state. Static and Bayesian comparators use same hypothesis universe; latent history source segments not exposed.
frozen_design.evaluator: Prequential Brier on 48 feedback outcomes per phase before labels, held Brier on 16 never-trained actions at B48 and return48, per-family and 128 paired related trials with normal 95% CI. Count false switches and first detection delays; report raw compute and A-retention.

mechanism.active_graph: Initialize selected source A mask by penalized LOO Brier. Every 8 post-source feedback events, evaluate adding, pruning or swapping one edge, selecting best neighbor using last <=32 events excluding latest 8; witness selection uses the latest 8 distinct-on-stream events not fitted into candidate. Stable A model immutable.
mechanism.switch_to_new: Enter B-mode when candidate using recent fit improves held-within-training witness Brier over A-source by >=0.025 and both 4-event witness halves improve; candidate must beat null baseline by >=0.005 on witnesses, no true boundary input. At most one graph mutation at any checkpoint; may continue local rewiring while in B-mode using same fit/witness test.
mechanism.return_to_A: While B-mode, if A-source beats active local candidate on latest witness eight by >=0.025 and two halves agree, reactivate original stored source A graph without changing A memory.
mechanism.cooldown: After any mode change, do not change mode for one further 8-event checkpoint. No behavior depends on true phase labels.
mechanism.predict: If source mode, use immutable A64 conditional-table probabilities; else use fitted active subset on last up-to-32 feedback stream events. Compare online prequential and never-trained phase holdout.
controls: independently implemented global static best subset fitted to all A+stream observed events every 8 feedback steps
independently implemented sliding-window 32-event global subset fit every 8 steps
Bayesian hazard soft mixture of source A and a recency-32 Beta-binomial 1..3-subset posterior, hazard=1/64, updated before label learning
ungated local greedy graph on same stream, no switch witness
0.5 null and oracle-known-phase segment graph only illustrative
mechanism.cold: Serialize A64 rows, up to 96 stream rows, source mask, active mask, mode, cooldown and counters in exactly 384 bytes at time 48, 72 and 96; restore into independent in-process instance and compare future actions, bytes and predictions. No true process-exit/native checkpoint claim.

negative_controls: source-A-only, global static, sliding recency, Bayesian hazard, ungated graph and random null

classification_rules.supported: All frozen thresholds PASS together, then still only preliminary synthetic DEVELOPMENT signal pending independent reproduction/native qualification.
classification_rules.mixed: Some positive but any frozen required threshold FAIL, SCIENTIFIC_NO_GO, preserve results.
classification_rules.negative: Stronger fully trained/Bayesian or noise negative defeats joint target, SCIENTIFIC_NO_GO.
classification_rules.invalid: Missing custody, wrong data/compute accounting, held leakage, violation of frozen protocol.
